Enderby, a small islet near Floreana, offers an introduction to the ocean side of the Galápagos. The main experiences here are connected with the water, reef wildlife and animals encountered on a marine excursion.

The program description lists Enderby among 3 possible dive sites in the Floreana area. Reef dives in this area are described as having an average depth of about 18 m, with coral and sponges. Sea lions, turtles, reef fish, rays and sharks may be seen. The dive site is selected together with the dive center; wildlife sightings and actual conditions depend on the ocean.

## Encarnación & Trinidad — a cultural center of Paraguay!

Encarnación is located on the border with Argentina and is Paraguay's second-largest city. It is a distinctive cultural center with a multinational population shaped by active immigration from Europe in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

## Encarnación & Trinidad — Paraguay's carnival city!

From the city, you can reach the nearby ruins of the Jesuit missions at Trinidad and Jesús. Today this modern, multifunctional city has excellent shops and attractive squares. When the enormous Yacyretá hydroelectric power station was built, a man-made reservoir extended as far as Encarnación, and businesses and offices were relocated to higher ground. Yet the old city retained many inexpensive market stalls selling colorful trinkets. One of Encarnación's streets leading down to the river has become an open-air museum and promenade, displaying old boats, navigation buoys, anchors and steam boilers from small steamships. Another attraction draws hundreds of tourists: unlike other Paraguayan cities, Encarnación holds an annual carnival.

At Ensenada Zaratiegui Bay, the forests of Tierra del Fuego reach the shores of the Beagle Channel. The stony beach and water against a backdrop of mountains offer a glimpse of the national park's maritime environment.

Ensenada is one of the accessible stops on an excursion route through the park. A coastal trail begins here. A short visit to the bay can be combined with a trip to Lake Roca and Lapataia, with the length of the walk chosen according to the travel program.

Ernesto Tornquist Provincial Park protects part of the Ventania mountain system in Buenos Aires Province. Its distinctive landscape of rocky ridges and grassy slopes contrasts sharply with the surrounding agricultural plains.

The protected area conserves mountain grasslands and watersheds, and supports species associated with this particular natural region. We offer guided walks through the park. The specific trail and viewpoints are selected according to the group's fitness, the weather and access regulations. The trip can conveniently be organized from Sierra de la Ventana, leaving time to relax after returning.

Española is one of the Galápagos islands where a walk turns into wildlife watching almost from the first steps. It is an old, low-lying, dry island in the south of the archipelago. Its rocky shores, patches of vegetation and surrounding ocean are home to birds, marine iguanas and sea lions.

At Punta Suárez, the natural world reveals itself in small scenes: an iguana warming itself on a rock, a bird surveying the shore, sea foam rising beside lava cliffs. During the breeding season, male marine iguanas here develop striking red-and-green coloring. They are best observed from a distance, while staying on the marked trail and allowing the animals to move freely.

The waved albatross holds a special place in Española's wildlife. The island is its principal breeding ground. In season, usually from April to December, these large birds with long yellow bills can be seen here. Their presence depends on when you travel, so an albatross-watching itinerary should be planned around the season.

Gardner Bay reveals a gentler side of the island: pale sand, clear water and sea lions resting on the shore. After the rocky trail at Punta Suárez, the beach scenery adds a different dimension to the trip. Española will particularly appeal to nature lovers and photographers willing to spend time observing a single bird, noticing the animals' movements and discovering the island through its inhabitants.
